title: The Most Quietly Beloved Show on Indian OTT Is Back. Gram Chikitsalay Returns June 23.
excerpt: TVF's slice-of-life rural drama brings Dr. Prabhat back to Bhathkandi — and this time the idealistic young doctor is up against bribes, bureaucracy, and a Bhojpuri superstar villain.
body:
There's a particular kind of Indian show that doesn't trend, doesn't get a billion-view trailer, doesn't have a star walking a red carpet in a backless gown — and yet lodges itself somewhere in your chest and refuses to leave. **Gram Chikitsalay** is one of those. And on June 23, it comes home.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=6YkxIy5QkwA</youtube>

**Prime Video** and **The Viral Fever** released the trailer for **Gram Chikitsalay Season 2** on Friday, and within its first minute it does the thing TVF does better than anyone: it makes a crumbling rural Primary Health Centre feel like the most important place in the world. **Amol Parashar** returns as **Dr. Prabhat Sinha**, the young, idealistic, slightly stubborn doctor who walked into the fictional village of Bhathkandi in Season 1 hoping to fix a neglected clinic — and slowly, painfully discovered that the building was the easy part.

> "In the latest chapter, my character's journey in Bhathkandi moves forward in unexpected ways. He has experienced some good wins, but a whole new set of challenges comes his way." — Amol Parashar

Parashar is the soul of this show, and it's worth saying plainly: he's never been better than when he's playing Prabhat. There's no movie-star swagger here, no item number, no slow-motion entry. Just a tired, decent man in a short-sleeved shirt trying to do his job inside a system designed to exhaust him. It's the least glamorous role imaginable, and Parashar makes it quietly magnetic. You watch his face do the math between what's right and what's possible, and you can't look away.

Season 2 raises the stakes in the most Indian way conceivable: a district-level competition for the coveted **'Adarsh PHC'** (model health centre) award. To win it, Dr. Prabhat has to navigate the swamp of local politics, chronic resource shortages, and the village's hardest currency of all — trust. Fixing the building was the easy part. Earning the faith of people who've been let down by the system their whole lives is the real fight.

The casting twist this season is delicious. **Dinesh Lal Yadav** — better known to millions as **Nirahua**, the colossus of Bhojpuri cinema — joins as Babu Saheb, a corrupt official who runs on bribes and obstruction. Putting a genuine regional superstar into TVF's understated, grounded world is an inspired bit of casting; Nirahua's larger-than-life presence rubbing up against the show's careful realism could be the season's most entertaining friction. Returning to round out the ensemble are **Vinay Pathak**, Akash Makhija, Anandeshwar Dwivedi, Akansha Ranjan Kapoor, and Garima Vikrant Singh, all reprising their Season 1 roles.

And then there's the Easter egg that sent the TVF faithful into a frenzy: the trailer features cameos by **Banrakas** (Durgesh Kumar) and Binod — characters straight out of *Panchayat*, TVF's other rural crown jewel. Whether it's a full crossover or a knowing wink, it confirms what fans have long suspected: these shows breathe the same dusty, golden-hour North Indian air. The TVF rural universe is real, and it's expanding.

Directed by **Lalitam Tiwari** and written by Vaibhav Suman and Shreya Srivastava, the new season holds fast to the gentle, unhurried storytelling that made the original a sleeper favourite. "Since season one, our aim has been to authentically capture rural life in all its realities," Tiwari said. "The new season builds on that vision by depicting the challenges of delivering healthcare, the quirks, deep community bonds, and resilience that define rural living."

For the diaspora, this one matters more than it might seem. **Gram Chikitsalay Season 2** premieres worldwide on **Prime Video on June 23, 2026**, streaming in Hindi across India and over 240 countries and territories. For NRIs raising kids in Edison or Hounslow or Brampton who want to show them an India that isn't all wedding sangeets and Mumbai skylines — an India of village clinics, monsoon mud, and small stubborn acts of decency — there is genuinely nothing better on streaming right now. It's the India your parents talk about, rendered with warmth instead of nostalgia.

No backless gowns. No 75-million-view trailer. Just one of the best, most humane shows India makes, returning to do it again. Bhatkandi jaane ke liye phir se taiyaar ho jaiye.
